fix(model-gateway): list only the Vibe models Vibe's config declares

vibeModels had only ever read config.toml's models as a table, but setup
writes them as an array of tables ([[models]], one entry per alias) -- so on
a machine whose configuration reads, the listing came back empty and every
shipped catalogue entry fell back into "models", marked declared. That is
why the gateway offered mistral-large-latest and friends that "vibe --model"
rejects. vibeModels now reads both shapes, and a catalogue entry a
successful Vibe listing does not match is no longer offered: it is reported
in "skipped" with a reason, so a model Vibe's config does not declare is
never listed.

The Vibe catalogue now names the aliases Vibe accepts: glm-5-3 (names
zai-glm-5-3), mistral-large-4-0-3 (names mistral-large-latest and
mistral-large-4-0), mistral-medium-3.5 and zai-glm-5-3-flash, its prices
from docs.mistral.ai/inference/pricing. The deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017 and
mistral-small-latest entries stay, for the prices of the critic agents
that still run them, and are now never offered while Vibe rejects them.

Critique routing: the vibe-mistral-large gateway route names
mistral-large-4-0-3, the alias Vibe accepts for the model its agent runs;
vibe-deepseek-flash and vibe-mistral-small name no gateway route, because
Vibe accepts no alias for their models, so the ledger counts their runs
under the model the agent really pinned. The vibe_critic_agents keep their
pinned model ids: each agent file carries its own [[models]] entry, which
Vibe resolves without the home's config.toml aliases, and their prices are
the published ones -- repinning them to what Vibe accepts now would move
critics onto models without a live check and lose the DeepSeek family.

model-gateway.mjs rebuilt; manifest hashes updated with it.
